description: The INITIALIZE THEN REPLACING connective - a 2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85's INITIALIZE is INITIALIZE {identifier-1}... with at most a REPLACING phrase (§1985:VI.6.17.2), 'The INITIALIZE statement provides the ability to set selected types of data fields to predetermined values' (§1985:VI.6.17.1), and its only phrase is REPLACING, 'The key word following the word REPLACING corresponds to a category of data' (§1985:VI.6.17.4 GR1), with no connective before it ('The same category cannot be repeated in a REPLACING phrase.', §1985:VI.6.17.3 SR3); the 2002 general format writes the phrase as THEN REPLACING category-name DATA BY {identifier-2 | literal-1}..., after the optional VALUE phrase (§2002:14.8.19.1), and keeps REPLACING's meaning, 'The REPLACING phrase is specified and the category of the elementary data item' is one of those named (§2002:14.8.19.3 GR5). THEN is an optional word that arrives with the 2002 format, whose new phrases §2002:F.2 records as items 72 (FILLER) and 73 (VALUE). 2014 and 2023 keep the format (§2014:14.9.19.1, §2023:14.9.20.2). Folded from the inline InitializeBinder gate (Exec Step E).
vcr: 2002 introduction (§2002:14.8.19.1 THEN REPLACING; REPLACING itself is §1985:VI.6.17)

PROGRAM-ID. RWITRP.
DATA DIVISION.

01 A PIC X(3) VALUE "ABC".

MAIN.
    INITIALIZE A THEN REPLACING ALPHANUMERIC DATA BY "Z".
    STOP RUN.
